fixes.explanation: That's the one, baker. Aaron, Moses' brother (Exodus 4:14), tells them, "Take off the gold earrings that are on your wives and sons and daughters, and bring them to me." (Exodus 32:2) Then all the people take off their gold earrings and bring them to Aaron (Exodus 32:3). That's a whole lot of jewelry heading in one direction.

Sandals, friend? That would be a whole different request. Aaron asks for gold earrings, the ones on their wives and sons and daughters (Exodus 32:2). Nobody in this story is digging through a pile of shoes.

A calf, baker. Aaron takes the gold from their hands, and with an engraving tool he fashions it into a molten calf (Exodus 32:4). Gold earrings go in, and a calf comes out. Then the people say, "These, O Israel, are your gods…"

A wall, baker? That's a lot of bricklaying for a man who's about to announce a feast. The text says Aaron built an altar before the calf (Exodus 32:5). Then he proclaimed, "Tomorrow shall be a feast to the LORD."

True, baker. The next day they arose, offered burnt offerings, and presented peace offerings. Then "…the people sat down to eat and drink and got up to indulge in revelry." (Exodus 32:6) Offerings first, then the party. Notice the order.

That's not what Moses says, friend. He asks, "Why should the Egyptians declare, ‘He brought them out with evil intent, to kill them in the mountains and wipe them from the face of the earth’?" (Exodus 32:12) His worry is about what the Egyptians might declare, and it's about evil intent, not about their gods winning. Then he asks the LORD to relent from doing harm.

Ruling Egypt isn't in the promise Moses quotes, baker. He reminds the LORD of the words, "I will make your descendants as numerous as the stars in the sky, and I will give your descendants all this land that I have promised…" (Exodus 32:13) Nothing in those words mentions ruling Egypt. It's descendants and the land.

Singing, baker. Joshua says to Moses, "The sound of war is in the camp." But Moses replies, "It is neither the cry of victory nor the cry of defeat; I hear the sound of singing!" (Exodus 32:17-18) Joshua heard war, and Moses heard something else. I think Joshua was about to get a very different kind of news.

Close, but Moses crosses that one out too, baker. He says, "It is neither the cry of victory nor the cry of defeat; I hear the sound of singing!" (Exodus 32:18) Joshua had said war. Moses says singing.

Not this time, baker. The text says Moses "…burned with anger and threw the tablets out of his hands, shattering them at the base of the mountain." (Exodus 32:19) He doesn't hand them to anybody. They break right there.

Evil, baker. Aaron says, "Do not be enraged, my lord. You yourself know that the people are intent on evil." (Exodus 32:22) That's his reply when Moses asks what the people did to him that he has led them into so great a sin (Exodus 32:21). Then Aaron tells Moses what the people said to him (Exodus 32:23).

Actually true, friend. Moses tells the Levites that "…the LORD has bestowed a blessing on you this day." (Exodus 32:29) He says it right after telling them they have been ordained for service to the LORD. It's a heavy day, and I think that makes the word blessing stand out.
